executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) and PAHO (October 2025-May 2026) reveal multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to circulate in the Americas region with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, representing a critical pandemic preparedness concern as a BSL-3 select agent. Mpox (clade activity in the Americas), Yellow Fever, Dengue, and Chikungunya are generating elevated epidemiological alerts, while pertussis resurgence and measles importation risk compound the public health burden. The simultaneous start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season alongside RSV co-circulation further strains regional health system capacity.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas combined with concurrent outbreaks of dengue, mpox, yellow fever, and measles resurgence represent the most pressing multi-threat public health emergency requiring coordinated regional response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
BSL-3 select agent with documented animal-to-human transmission potential
Ongoing poultry and wild bird reservoir activity across Americas
Pandemic preparedness alert status maintained across reporting period
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce PPE protocols for exposed agricultural workers; sequence all human cases for antigen drift monitoring; pre-position antiviral stockpiles and H5-candidate vaccines

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating active transmission
BSL-3 select agent requiring enhanced containment measures
Sustained community transmission concern in Americas following global clade expansion
Ongoing vaccination coverage gaps in high-risk populations
threats.action: Expand ring vaccination and targeted immunization of high-risk groups; strengthen case detection and contact tracing; ensure laboratory diagnostic capacity at BSL-3 level; coordinate with ECDC on imported case surveillance

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 during historically high transmission period
Multi-serotype co-circulation risk increasing severe dengue probability
Early 2026 reporting follows record 2024-2025 dengue seasons in the Americas
Vector control gaps and urbanization sustaining Aedes aegypti populations
threats.action: Intensify integrated vector management; expand serotype surveillance to detect secondary infection clusters; strengthen severe dengue case management capacity; issue travel advisories for endemic zones

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 13 March 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Epizootic activity in non-human primates serving as amplification signal
Vaccination coverage gaps in at-risk populations and border zones
Potential for urban transmission cycle via Aedes aegypti if imported to unvaccinated urban areas
threats.action: Verify and strengthen yellow fever vaccination coverage in endemic and at-risk countries; enhance epizootic surveillance in primate populations; enforce vaccination requirements for travelers entering endemic zones; prepare response stockpiles

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Start)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere season
Simultaneous RSV co-circulation alert issued January 2026 indicating dual respiratory burden
Risk of health system strain from concurrent influenza and RSV surge
Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season transition overlap increasing surveillance complexity
threats.action: Maximize influenza vaccination uptake before peak season; strengthen sentinel surveillance and virological typing; prepare ICU surge capacity; monitor for antigenic mismatch between circulating strains and vaccine composition

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates within three months (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating accelerating trend
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy
Infant and neonatal mortality risk in undervaccinated communities
Potential AMR concern with macrolide-resistant B. pertussis strains emerging globally
threats.action: Audit and strengthen DTP/Tdap vaccination coverage especially in pregnant women and infants; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity to distinguish from other respiratory illness; review outbreak response protocols in high-risk districts

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating importation and transmission risk
Coverage gaps following COVID-19 pandemic disruptions to routine immunization
Americas region previously achieved measles elimination status now under threat
ECDC weekly reports likely tracking imported cases from Americas and other regions into Europe
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments and catch-up campaigns; strengthen measles case-based surveillance and laboratory confirmation; enforce outbreak response vaccination within 72 hours of case detection; coordinate with ECDC on cross-regional importation risk

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026 indicating active transmission
Geographic expansion of Aedes albopictus enabling spread into previously unaffected areas
Risk of chronic arthralgia burden in affected populations
Co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis and case management
threats.action: Enhance arboviral integrated surveillance distinguishing CHIKV from dengue; strengthen vector control in affected municipalities; train clinicians on differential diagnosis; monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable populations

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been detected and are generating active epidemiological alerts: (1) Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — the highest priority threat, with multiple PAHO updates in November 2025 and March 2026 documenting sustained animal reservoir activity and zoonotic spillover risk across the Americas, requiring BSL-3 laboratory handling and pandemic preparedness activation; (2) Monkeypox virus (MPXV) — active community transmission documented in the Americas as of April 2026, classified as a BSL-3 agent requiring enhanced containment, contact tracing, and targeted vaccination. Both agents require coordination between public health authorities, veterinary services, and laboratory networks operating at appropriate biosafety containment levels.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance risk noted given resurgence despite vaccination — warrants azithromycin susceptibility monitoring in outbreak settings
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) monitoring required for H5N1 strains given potential pandemic preparedness implications
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (February 2026) may indicate counterfeit pharmaceutical supply chains that could harbor antimicrobial contaminants or resistance-promoting compounds
emergingPatterns: Concurrent multi-arboviral circulation (Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever) in the Americas suggests expanding Aedes vector habitat driven by climate and urbanization factors
Dual epidemiological alert pattern for pertussis (December 2025 and March 2026) indicates accelerating resurgence consistent with post-pandemic immunization debt across the Americas
Simultaneous Southern Hemisphere influenza season start coinciding with RSV surge creates compound respiratory emergency risk and health system strain
H5N1 continued multi-month surveillance alert status suggests enzootic establishment in Americas bird populations beyond seasonal epizootic patterns
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20) during April-May 2026 suggests sustained elevated threat environment in Europe requiring ongoing monitoring
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 medication misuse alert (February 2026) indicate emerging non-infectious public health threats intersecting with health system capacity
